subject.title: [Feature]: Make Skill Workshop extensible for custom skill creation workflows

question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class skill-creation authority or pre-selection workflow hook for custom skill creation, and if so should it live in plugin hooks, tool policy/config, or a ClawHub workflow convention?
rationale: Current code already has Skill Workshop as a proposal primitive plus generic tool policy and `before_tool_call` hooks, but none of those establish the product contract for making a custom workflow run before `skill_workshop` is selected.

options.title: Design a first-class authority seam
options.body: Add a maintainer-owned plugin/config contract for skill-creation routing while keeping Skill Workshop as the only persistence boundary.

options.title: Document policy-only composition
options.body: Keep current APIs and document that operators must hide `skill_workshop` and expose their custom tool when they want a custom creation flow.

options.title: Defer to ClawHub/meta workflows
options.body: Treat custom skill creation workflows as external skill/plugin packages until a broader meta-skill direction is accepted.

recommendation.title: Design a first-class authority seam
recommendation.body: Add a maintainer-owned plugin/config contract for skill-creation routing while keeping Skill Workshop as the only persistence boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: The likely decision sits closest to the Skill Workshop write-boundary and lifecycle ownership shown in recent history.
